1069030033308770305.a: Posit this, humans inherently are not anti-nature. Changing the landscape and using resources is natural. Humans are non-natural compared to many animals, though. That is, human nature seems to be a compliment to animal nature. We are thinking engineers. Animals rely on instinct.

1069030035091324928.a: Amazon rainforests seem to be a good example. The ancient landscape seems to be engineered by ancient humans. Bears, cats, wolves, etc will naturally create a fertile landscape given time. Humans can engineer a fertile landscape rather than leave it to chance. Or destroy it.

1069030037301706752.a: On a long enough time scale any species which wishes to survive must be able to engineer sustainable landscapes and environments. That includes turning barren rocks in space into habitable places, presumably. Or consigning the species to living inside artificial pods.

1069030038857834496.a: I find it interesting that so many people cannot see past their own lifetime or even next week. Indigenous peoples have this long vision and are keenly aware of their place in the universe. As I age & learn more history it seems short-sightedness is a deliberate control mechanism

1069360581260558336.a: Through time you find many claims as to how humans differ from animals. There are not many answers when probed deeply. Systematic preservation and sharing of knowledge is a major feature lacking in animals. This allows all humans to grow beyond the capability of one or few humans

1069360582321758208.a: I don't think it's strictly a biological feature. If anything, I suspect our biology evolved to improve it. Once gorillas learn to communicate effectively it seems like they begin to share information similarly but lack the evolution to do it well. Conjecture on my part, clearly.

1069360583668129793.a: My point, if there is one, is that breakdowns in society occur when small groups try to share false information or hoard the truth for themselves. Humans flourish in the presence of truth. If it's bad news we tend to share more vigorously to solve it. Animals go extinct. Will we?

1069361949673209856.a: The current political climate reminds me of a story I recall of a gorilla who learned human sign language. Released to live with gorillas who only knew their limited gorilla gestures. This gorilla kept trying to share its own knowledge to improve the others lives but was ignored.
